name: Exterior Painting Scope of Work for Stucco Homes in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What should a detailed exterior painting scope of work include for a stucco house in Los Angeles County to avoid change orders later?
mainEntity.text: What should a detailed exterior painting scope of work include for a stucco house in Los Angeles County to avoid change orders later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many exterior painting quotes in Los Angeles County are one-page estimates with vague language like “prep and paint,” which often leads to change orders once work begins. A protective scope of work for a stucco home should list each major step as a line item. Under preparation, specify power-washing or soft-washing methods, how efflorescence and chalking will be treated, and whether loose or failing paint will be scraped, sanded, or ground out. For stucco repair, describe how hairline, medium, and structural cracks will be handled, and who pays for unforeseen larger patches. Include product names, manufacturers, and number of coats for primer and finish paint, plus estimated spread rates. Note whether elastomeric coatings will be used on problem walls. Define masking and protection: which windows, landscaping, roof tiles, and fixtures will be covered and how overspray is controlled. Clarify access: ladders vs. scaffolding vs. lifts and who is responsible for permits, if any. Finally, list exclusions such as dry-rot repair, termite damage, lead remediation, or replacing damaged trim. Request this level of detail from each contractor so you can compare bids fairly and reduce surprises during the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: A detailed exterior painting scope for a Los Angeles stucco home should spell out substrate repairs, crack treatment methods, number of coats, exact products, surface prep steps, masking areas, access methods, and excluded items. Clear line items greatly reduce surprise change orders and help compare contractor bids accurately.
